item.title: NASA exploring EarthDaily data to complement Landsat
item.description: WASHINGTON — EarthDaily’s recent contract to validate the quality and compatibility of its data with NASA’s Landsat imaging constellation could offer the civil space agency a complementary commercial source for Earth observation and analytics.

item.title: China’s first commercial lunar missions take shape
item.description: HELSINKI — Two Chinese commercial companies are developing lunar spacecraft, signalling the start of a new phase in the country’s moon exploration efforts.

item.title: Is faster and cheaper really better for NASA science?
item.description: Since NASA Administrator Dan Goldin introduced the concept of “faster, better, cheaper” to the agency in the 1990s, a debate has raged: Can smaller missions, which are faster and less expensive to develop but carry a higher risk of failure, be as effective as larger flagship missions, which have been prone to major cost and schedule overruns?

item.title: Quantum Space goes public
item.description: Quantum Space, a company developing highly maneuverable spacecraft and led by a former NASA administrator, started trading publicly Nov. 24 after completing a merger.

item.title: Small nations don’t need a Space Force. They need the right space organization.
item.description: The establishment of the United States Space Force, China’s Aerospace Force and France’s Space Command has prompted political and military leaders to consider creating similar organizations. For small and medium-sized states, that temptation is a trap. Recognizing space as a warfighting domain compels smaller states to develop military space organizations — but not as national symbols. The main limitations are the strategic position of these small states and their budgets to build and sustain such organizations. For small and medium-sized states, creating a military space organization involves an opportunity cost. Resources could alternatively be allocated to building more combat units or acquiring additional tanks, aircraft and ships. On the other hand, a smaller military space organization may be a force multiplier to help the mission.

item.title: White House seeks an additional $2 billion for Artemis in 2027
item.description: The White House is asking Congress to provide up to $2 billion in additional funding for NASA’s Artemis program, but with few details about how the money should be spent.

item.title: European companies seek supporting roles on orbital data center projects
item.description: As American and Chinese companies advance plans to develop orbital data centers, European firms are looking for ways to support those efforts rather than compete directly.

item.title: Satellite maker EnduroSat books two dedicated New Glenn launches
item.description: EnduroSat has booked two dedicated New Glenn launches starting in 2029 for the Bulgarian satellite maker’s customers as the industry prepares for the end of SpaceX’s Falcon 9 rideshare program.

item.title: First international astronaut arrives at Tiangong on Shenzhou-24
item.description: HELSINKI — A Pakistani astronaut arrived at China’s Tiangong space station Wednesday, the first foreign national to fly on a Chinese spacecraft and visit the orbital outpost.

item.title: Private equity firm Cerberus to acquire Airbus’ U.S. satellite business
item.description: The deal brings a factory built for OneWeb’s broadband constellation under American ownership.

item.title: A reset in the military spending debate
item.description: The immediate question is whether Congress can agree on a fiscal 2027 defense budget, and how long the Pentagon and its contractors might have to wait.

item.title: Ariane 6 launches fourth set of Amazon Leo satellites
item.description: An Ariane 6 successfully launched three dozen Amazon Leo satellites, the first satellites for that constellation to reach orbit in four and a half months.

item.title: BlackSky acquires data firm EpochGeo
item.description: WASHINGTON — BlackSky Technology announced it acquired geospatial data firm EpochGeo, a move to expand its slate of real-time intelligence tools as defense customers seek deeper analysis and data fusion capabilities.

item.title: Russia launches Progress cargo spacecraft to ISS with unusual secrecy
item.description: Russia launched a Progress cargo spacecraft to the International Space Station Nov. 24 under an unusual level of secrecy assisted by NASA.

item.description: The company’s Portal system sent commands to and received telemetry from a government satellite

item.title: Umbra unveils new family of SAR satellites
item.description: WASHINGTON — Space technology company Umbra unveiled a new line of synthetic aperture radar (SAR) satellites that the company says will bring improved accuracy and an expanded capability set.

item.title: Space Beyond orders hardware for 10 more memorial cubesat missions
item.description: Space Beyond has ordered enough hardware for 10 follow-on cubesats after growing sales for the Florida startup’s first memorial spacecraft, slated to carry cremated remains into orbit in October 2027.

item.title: Upgrading cellular networks with space support
item.description: Using satellites to connect smartphones beyond the reach of cell towers is not the only way the space industry can help cellular operators plug coverage gaps.

item.title: Thruster glitch clouds BepiColombo arrival at Mercury
item.description: A joint European-Japanese mission has entered orbit around Mercury after an eight-year journey, but a premature shutdown of its thrusters has raised questions about its orbit.

item.title: With the proliferation of European satellites, we need a new approach to space-based surveillance
item.description: European space companies are expanding rapidly. They are attracting substantial investment, developing new satellite services and competing for contracts once reserved for large aerospace groups. But as more satellites enter low Earth orbit (LEO), operators face a growing problem: how can they monitor and protect the spacecraft on which communications, navigation, financial transactions and national security increasingly depend?

item.title: Europe’s space community makes the case for a human spaceflight program
item.description: European government officials and companies are building the case for Europe to invest in a human spaceflight capability ahead of a key meeting next month.

item.title: PiLogic testing satellite fault-prediction platform with SpaceWERX
item.description: WASHINGTON — PiLogic, a Los Angeles-based startup developing software to predict satellite failures and make spacecraft more autonomous, is working with SpaceWERX to test that capability on orbit.

item.title: Vyoma contracts Scanway to develop optical in-space monitoring systems for Kepler satellites
item.description: WARSAW, Poland — Scanway, an optical systems manufacturer based in Poland, has signed a contract with the German space domain awareness company Vyoma to develop optical instruments for an orbital object monitoring system. Scanway’s instruments will be incorporated into sensors that Vyoma plans to deploy on satellites operated by Canada-based Kepler Communications.

item.title: Landspace qualifies recovered Zhuque-3 engines for reuse after hot-fire tests
item.description: HELSINKI — Landspace has conducted hot-fire tests of nine engines from its recovered Zhuque-3 first stage and qualified them for reuse, marking a step toward reusability.
